title: Ensure all internal user storage APFS volumes are encrypted
description: Apple developed the APFS (Apple File System) structure primarily for flash and solid- state drives. This file structure was first made available in 10.12 and then became the default in 10.13. macOS computers generally have several volumes created as part of APFS formatting, including Preboot, Recovery and Virtual Memory (VM), as well as traditional user disks. All APFS volumes that do not have specific roles and do not require encryption should be encrypted. "Role" disks include Preboot, Recovery and VM. User disks are labelled with "(No specific role)" by default. In order to protect user data from loss or tampering volumes, carrying data should be encrypted.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure all internal user storage APFS volumes are encrypted

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/sbin/diskutil ] || exit 1
out=$(/usr/sbin/diskutil list internal | /usr/bin/grep 'APFS Volume' | /usr/bin/awk '{print $NF}' | /usr/bin/xargs -n1 /usr/sbin/diskutil info | /usr/bin/grep -E "Volume Name|FileVault" | /usr/bin/sed '/Preboot/{N;d;}' | /usr/bin/sed '/Recovery/{N;d;}' | /usr/bin/sed '/VM/{N;d;}')
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qE 'FileVault: +No'; then printf '%s\n' "$out"; else echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Use Disk Utility to erase a user disk and format as APFS (Encrypted). Note: APFS Encrypted disks will be described as "FileVault" whether they are the boot volume or not in the ap list.

title: Ensure all APFS and HFS+ external user storage volumes are encrypted
description: Apple developed the APFS (Apple File System) structure primarily for flash and solid- state drives. This file structure was first made available in 10.12 and then became the default in 10.13. Apple introduced CoreStorage with Mac OS X 10.7 Lion. It is used as the default for formatting on macOS volumes prior to macOS 10.13 High Sierra. All HFS and CoreStorage Volumes should be encrypted. CoreStorage has been deprecated and replaced with APFS for volume encryption. In order to protect user data from loss or tampering volumes, carrying data should be encrypted.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.3.2 Ensure all APFS and HFS+ external user storage volumes are encrypted

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/sbin/diskutil ] || exit 1
out=$(/usr/sbin/diskutil list external | /usr/bin/grep -E 'APFS Volume|Apple_HFS|Logical Volume' | /usr/bin/awk '{print $NF}' | /usr/bin/xargs -n1 /usr/sbin/diskutil info | /usr/bin/grep -E "Volume Name|FileVault")
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qE 'FileVault: +No'; then printf '%s\n' "$out"; else echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Use Disk Utility to erase a user disk and format as APFS (Encrypted). Note: It is recommended using APFS over HFS+ where possible. If you do need to use an HFS+/CoreStorage external drive for compatibility reasons, you need to format the drive to MacOS Extended (Journaled) (or MacOS Extended (Case-Sensitive, Journaled) if Case-Sensitive is required).

title: Ensure the Sudo Timeout Period Is Set to Zero
description: The sudo command allows the user to run programs as the root user. Working as the root user allows the user an extremely high level of configurability within the system. This control, along with the control to use a separate timestamp for each tty, limits the window where an unauthorized user, process, or attacker could utilize legitimate credentials that are valid for longer than required. The sudo command stays logged in as the root user for five minutes before timing out and re-requesting a password. This five-minute window should be eliminated since it leaves the system extremely vulnerable. This is especially true if an exploit were to gain access to the system, since they would be able to make changes as a root user.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.4 Ensure the Sudo Timeout Period Is Set to Zero

audit.command:
v=$(/usr/bin/sudo -V 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
c=$(printf '%s\n' "$v" | /usr/bin/grep -c "Authentication timestamp timeout: 0.0 minutes")
o=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Su:%Sg' /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$c" -ge 1 ] && [ "$o" = root:wheel ]; then echo compliant; else echo "timeout-zero=$c owner=$o"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal Method: Run the following command to edit the sudo settings: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/sbin/visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/<configuration file name> example: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/sbin/visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/10_cissudoconfiguration Note: Unlike other Unix and/or Linux distros, macOS will ignore configuration files in the sudoers.d folder that contain a . so do not add a file extension to the configuration file. Add the line Defaults timestamp_timeout=0 to the configuration file. If /etc/sudoers.d/ is not owned by root or in the wheel group, run the following to change ownership and group: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/sbin/chown -R root:wheel /etc/sudoers.d/

title: Ensure the "root" Account Is Disabled
description: The root account is a superuser account that has access privileges to perform any actions and read/write to any file on the computer. With some versions of Linux, the system administrator may commonly use the root account to perform administrative functions. Previous versions of the benchmark included a graphical check for the audit and remediation as well as a different Terminal command for the remediation. After extensive testing, it was discovered that if root was enabled it could be granted a secure token which was not removed with the previous remediation. To rectify this issue, the audit was updated to verify if root has a secure token even if the root account is not enabled. The remediation was also updated to remove root's secure token as well as an updated command to disable the root user. Enabling and using the root account puts the system at risk since any successful exploi...
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.6 Ensure the "root" Account Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/dscl . -read /Users/root AuthenticationAuthority 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -q "No such key: AuthenticationAuthority" && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Terminal Method: Run the following commands to disable the root user: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/fdesetup remove -user root 2>/dev/null % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/dscl /Local/Default delete /Users/root AuthenticationAuthority

title: Ensure an Administrator Account Cannot Login to Another User's Active and Locked Session
description: macOS has a privilege that can be granted to any user that will allow that user to unlock active users' sessions. Disabling the administrator's and/or user's ability to log into another user's active and locked session prevents unauthorized persons from viewing potentially sensitive and/or personal information.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.7 Ensure an Administrator Account Cannot Login to Another User's Active and Locked Session

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/security authorizationdb read system.login.screensaver 2>&1) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/awk -F "[<>]" '$3=="authenticate-session-owner" { ++x } END { print x+0 }'

remediation.guidance: Terminal Method: Run the following command to disable a user logging into another user's active and/or locked session: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/security authorizationdb write system.login.screensaver authenticate-session-owner YES (0) Running this command will disable Touch ID to unlock the screen saver. To re-enable Touch ID for users, run the following command: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow screenUnlockMode -int 1

title: Ensure the Guest Home Folder Does Not Exist
description: In the previous two controls, the guest account login has been disabled and sharing to guests has been disabled, as well. There is no need for the legacy Guest home folder to remain in the file system. When normal user accounts are removed, you have the option to archive it, leave it in place, or delete. In the case of the guest folder, the folder remains in place without a GUI option to remove it. If at some point in the future a Guest account is needed, it will be re-created. The presence of the Guest home folder can cause automated audits to fail when looking for compliant settings within all User folders, as well. Rather than ignoring the folder's continued existence, it is best removed. The Guest home folders are unneeded after the Guest account is disabled and could be used inappropriately.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.9 Ensure the Guest Home Folder Does Not Exist

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/ls /Users/ 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -cx Guest || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal Method: Run the following command to remove the Guest user home folder: % /usr/bin/sudo /bin/rm -R /Users/Guest Note: If the Guest folder exists it maybe a legacy folder. If so, the folder should be removed. If you are unsure if the Guest folder is a legacy folder, then your organization should research why that folder is there. Also research what is contained (or was contained) within it before removing the folder.

title: Ensure XProtect Is Running and Updated
description: XProtect is Apple's native signature-based antivirus technology. XProtect both finds and blocks the execution of known malware. There are many AV and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools available for macOS. The native Apple provisioned tool looks for specific known malware and is completely integrated into the OS. No matter what other tools are being used, XProtect should have the latest signatures available. Apple creates signatures for known malware that actually affects Macs and that knowledge should be leveraged.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 14.0 Sonoma Benchmark v3.1.0 - 5.10 Ensure XProtect Is Running and Updated

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/xprotect status 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
if printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -q "XProtect launch scans: enabled" && printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -q "XProtect background scans: enabled"; then echo compliant; else printf '%s
' "$out"; fi

remediation.command: Terminal Method: Run the following command to enable and update XProtect: % /usr/bin/sudo /bin/launchctl load -w /Library/Apple/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.XProtect.daemon.scan.pl ist % /usr/bin/sudo /bin/launchctl load -w /Library/Apple/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.XprotectFramework.Plugi nService.plist % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/xprotect update Starting update. Update succeeded: Activated update LocalUpdate[<newest XProtect version>] Note: XProtect can only be enabled/disabled if SIP (System Integrity Protection) is disabled. If XProtect is disabled, the system might be compromised and needs to be investigated.

title: Ensure Apple-provided Software Updates Are Installed
description: Software vendors release security patches and software updates for their products when security vulnerabilities are discovered. There is no simple way to complete this action without a network connection to an Apple software repository. Please ensure appropriate access for this control. This check is only for what Apple provides through software update. Audit: Passes when LastFullSuccessfulDate is within 30 days and RecommendedUpdates lists no pending update.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.1 Ensure Apple-provided Software Updates Are Installed

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/defaults ] || exit 1
d=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate LastFullSuccessfulDate 2>/dev/null) || { echo "never checked"; exit 0; }
t=$(/bin/date -j -f "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z" "$d" +%s 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
now=$(/bin/date +%s)
[ $((now - t)) -le 2592000 ] || { echo "last successful check older than 30 days: $d"; exit 0; }
n=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate RecommendedUpdates 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c "Product Key")
if [ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "updates pending: $n"; fi

remediation.command: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate -l ; sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate -i -a ; sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate -i '<package name>'. GUI: System Settings > General > Software Update > Update All.

title: Ensure Install Security Responses and System Files Is Enabled
description: Ensure that system and security updates are installed after they are available from Apple. This setting enables definition updates for XProtect and Gatekeeper. With this setting in place, new malware and adware that Apple has added to the list of malware or untrusted software will not execute. These updates do not require reboots or end user admin rights.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.5 Ensure Install Security Responses and System Files Is Enabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.SoftwareUpdate ConfigDataInstall = <true/>; com.apple.SoftwareUpdate CriticalUpdateInstall = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate ConfigDataInstall -bool true ; sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate CriticalUpdateInstall -bool true. GUI: System Settings > General > Software Update > i > Set Install Security Responses and System files to enabled > Done.

title: Ensure Software Update Deferment Is Less Than or Equal to 30 Days
description: Apple provides the capability to manage software updates on Apple devices through mobile device management. Part of those capabilities permit organizations to defer software updates and allow for testing. Many organizations have specialized software and configurations that may be negatively impacted by Apple updates. If software updates are deferred, they should not be deferred for more than 30 days. Audit: No deferral profile (no value) passes, as the benchmark states.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.6 Ensure Software Update Deferment Is Less Than or Equal to 30 Days

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess enforcedSoftwareUpdateDelay = <integer><1-30></integer>.

title: Ensure Firewall Is Enabled
description: A firewall is a piece of software that blocks unwanted incoming connections to a system. The socketfilter Firewall is what is used when the Firewall is turned on in the Security & Privacy Preference Pane. Logging is required to appropriately monitor what access is allowed and denied. The logs can be viewed in the macOS Unified Logs. Audit: Passes when the com.apple.security.firewall EnableFirewall key is true or socketfilterfw reports State = 1 or 2.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.2.1 Ensure Firewall Is Enabled

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/osascript ] || exit 1
p=$(/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.security.firewall').objectForKey('EnableFirewall').js
EOS
)
s=$(/usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --getglobalstate 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$p" = true ] || printf '%s' "$s" | /usr/bin/grep -qE 'State = [12]'; then echo compliant; else echo "EnableFirewall=${p:-unset}; $s"; fi

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.security.firewall EnableFirewall = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on. GUI: System Settings > Network > Firewall > Set Firewall to enabled.

title: Ensure Firewall Stealth Mode Is Enabled
description: While in Stealth mode, the computer will not respond to unsolicited probes, dropping that traffic. Audit: Passes when EnableStealthMode is true in a profile or socketfilterfw reports stealth mode on.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.2.2 Ensure Firewall Stealth Mode Is Enabled

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/osascript ] || exit 1
p=$(/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.security.firewall').objectForKey('EnableStealthMode').js
EOS
)
s=$(/usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --getstealthmode 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$p" = true ] || printf '%s' "$s" | /usr/bin/grep -q 'stealth mode is on'; then echo compliant; else echo "EnableStealthMode=${p:-unset}; $s"; fi

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.security.firewall EnableStealthMode = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setstealthmode on. GUI: System Settings > Network > Firewall > Options > Set Enabled stealth mode to enabled.

title: Ensure Screen Sharing Is Disabled
description: Screen Sharing allows a computer to connect to another computer on a network and display the computer’s screen. While sharing the computer’s screen, the user can control what happens on that computer, such as opening documents or applications, opening, moving, or closing windows, and even shutting down the computer.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.1 Ensure Screen Sharing Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -cE 'com.apple.screensharing$' || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl disable system/com.apple.screensharing ; sudo /bin/launchctl bootout system/com.apple.screensharing. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Screen Sharing to disabled.

title: Ensure File Sharing Is Disabled
description: File sharing from a user workstation creates additional risks, such as: • Open ports are created that can be probed and attacked • Passwords are attached to user accounts for access that may be exposed and endanger other parts of the organizational environment, including directory accounts • Increased complexity makes security more difficult and may expose additional attack vectors Apple's File Sharing uses the...
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.2 Ensure File Sharing Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c 'com.apple.smbd' || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl disable system/com.apple.smbd ; sudo /bin/launchctl bootout system/com.apple.smbd. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set File Sharing to disabled.

title: Ensure Remote Login Is Disabled
description: Remote Login allows an interactive terminal connection to a computer. Audit: All three benchmark checks must pass: systemsetup reports Off, sshd is disabled in launchd and not running.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.4 Ensure Remote Login Is Disabled

audit.command:
a=$(/usr/sbin/systemsetup -getremotelogin 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
b=$(/bin/launchctl print-disabled system 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c '"com.openssh.sshd" => disabled')
c=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c "com.openssh.sshd")
if printf '%s' "$a" | /usr/bin/grep -q "Remote Login: Off" && [ "$b" -eq 1 ] && [ "$c" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "$a; disabled=$b; running=$c"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setremotelogin off. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Remote Login to disabled.

title: Ensure Remote Management Is Disabled
description: Remote Management is the client portion of Apple Remote Desktop (ARD). Remote Management can be used by remote administrators to view the current screen, install software, report on, and generally manage client Macs. The screen sharing options in Remote Management are identical to those in the Screen Sharing section. In fact, only one of the two can be configured. Audit: Passes when no ARDAgent process is running.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.5 Ensure Remote Management Is Disabled

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/sw_vers ] || exit 1
out=$(/bin/ps -axo comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c ARDAgent || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /System/Library/CoreServices/RemoteManagement/ARDAgent.app/Contents/Resources /kickstart -deactivate -stop. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Remote Management to disabled.

title: Ensure Remote Apple Events Is Disabled
description: Apple Events is a technology that allows one program to communicate with other programs. Remote Apple Events allows a program on one computer to communicate with a program on a different computer.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.6 Ensure Remote Apple Events Is Disabled

audit.command: /usr/sbin/systemsetup -getremoteappleevents 2>/dev/null

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setremoteappleevents off. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Remote Apple Events to disabled.

title: Ensure Internet Sharing Is Disabled
description: Internet Sharing uses the open source natd process to share an internet connection with other computers and devices on a local network. This allows the Mac to function as a router and share the connection to other, possibly unauthorized, devices. Audit: Passes when com.apple.nat has no "Enabled = 1" entry or a profile sets forceInternetSharingOff.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.7 Ensure Internet Sharing Is Disabled

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/defaults ] || exit 1
f=$(/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.MCX').objectForKey('forceInternetSharingOff').js
EOS
)
n=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/com.apple.nat 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c "Enabled = 1;")
if [ "$f" = true ] || [ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "Internet Sharing enabled"; fi

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX forceInternetSharingOff = <true/>. Terminal: usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/com.apple.nat NAT -dict Enabled -int 0. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Internet Sharing to disabled.

title: Ensure Time Machine Volumes Are Encrypted If Time Machine Is Enabled
description: One of the most important security tools for data protection on macOS is FileVault. With encryption in place, it makes it difficult for an outside party to access your data if they get physical possession of the computer. One very large weakness in data protection with FileVault is the level of protection on backup volumes. Audit: Time Machine not configured counts as compliant (no NotEncrypted destination).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.4.2 Ensure Time Machine Volumes Are Encrypted If Time Machine Is Enabled

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/defaults ] || exit 1
out=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.TimeMachine.plist 2>/dev/null)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c NotEncrypted || true

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Time Machine > unencrypted drive > - to forget that drive as a destination > + to add a different drive as the destination > Set Up Disk > Set Encrypt Backup to enabled > Enter a password in the New Password and the same password in the Re-enter Password fields > A password hint is required, but it is recommended that you do not use any identifying information for the password.

title: Ensure Gatekeeper Is Enabled
description: Gatekeeper is Apple’s application that utilizes allowlisting to restrict downloaded applications from launching. It functions as a control to limit applications from unverified sources from running without authorization. In an update to Gatekeeper in macOS 13 Ventura, Gatekeeper checks every application on every launch, not just quarantined apps.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.5 Ensure Gatekeeper Is Enabled

audit.command: /usr/sbin/spctl --status 2>&1

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.systempolicy.control AllowIdentifiedDevelopers = <true/>; com.apple.systempolicy.control EnableAssessment = <true/>. GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Set 'Allow apps downloaded from' to 'App Store and identified developers'.

title: Ensure FileVault Is Enabled
description: FileVault secures a system's data by automatically encrypting its boot volume and requiring a password or recovery key to access it. FileVault should be used with a saved escrow key to ensure that the owner can decrypt their data if the password is lost. FileVault may also be enabled using command line using the fdesetup command. Audit: Requires FileVault On and the com.apple.MCX dontAllowFDEDisable profile key (the benchmark requires the profile).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.6 Ensure FileVault Is Enabled

audit.command:
s=$(/usr/bin/fdesetup status 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
p=$(/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.MCX').objectForKey('dontAllowFDEDisable').js
EOS
)
if printf '%s' "$s" | /usr/bin/grep -q "FileVault is On" && [ "$p" = true ]; then echo compliant; else echo "$s dontAllowFDEDisable=${p:-unset}"; fi

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX dontAllowFDEDisable = <true/>. GUI: System Settings > Security & Privacy > Turn On.

title: Ensure an Administrator Password Is Required to Access System-Wide Preferences
description: System Preferences controls system and user settings on a macOS Computer. System Preferences allows the user to tailor their experience on the computer as well as allowing the System Administrator to configure global security settings. Some of the settings should only be altered by the person responsible for the computer.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.8 Ensure an Administrator Password Is Required to Access System-Wide Preferences

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/security ] || exit 1
authDBs=("system.preferences" "system.preferences.energysaver" "system.preferences.network" "system.preferences.printing" "system.preferences.sharing" "system.preferences.softwareupdate" "system.preferences.startupdisk" "system.preferences.timemachine")
result="1"
for section in "${authDBs[@]}"; do
  if [[ $(/usr/bin/security -q authorizationdb read "$section" | /usr/bin/xmllint -xpath 'name(//*[contains(text(), "shared")]/following-sibling::*[1])' -) != "false" ]]; then
    result="0"
  fi
  if [[ $(/usr/bin/security -q authorizationdb read "$section" | /usr/bin/xmllint -xpath '//*[contains(text(), "group")]/following-sibling::*[1]/text()' -) != "admin" ]]; then
    result="0"
  fi
  if [[ $(/usr/bin/security -q authorizationdb read "$section" | /usr/bin/xmllint -xpath 'name(//*[contains(text(), "authenticate-user")]/following-sibling::*[1])' -) != "true" ]]; then
    result="0"
  fi
  if [[ $(/usr/bin/security -q authorizationdb read "$section" | /usr/bin/xmllint -xpath 'name(//*[contains(text(), "session-owner")]/following-sibling::*[1])' -) != "false" ]]; then
    result="0"
  fi
done
echo "$result"

remediation.guidance: Terminal: authDBs=("system.preferences" "system.preferences.energysaver" "system.preferences.network" "system.preferences.printing" "system.preferences.sharing" "system.preferences.softwareupdate" "system.preferences.startupdisk" "system.preferences.timemachine"). GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Advanced > Set Require an administrator password to access system-wide settings to enabled.

title: Ensure Require Password After Screen Saver Begins or Display Is Turned Off Is Enabled for 5 Seconds or Immediately
description: Sleep and screen saver modes are low power modes that reduce electrical consumption while the system is not in use. Audit: Passes when sysadminctl reports immediate/5 seconds for the console user or a profile sets askForPassword with askForPasswordDelay <= 5.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.11.2 Ensure Require Password After Screen Saver Begins or Display Is Turned Off Is Enabled for 5 Seconds or Immediately

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.screensaver askForPassword = <true/>; com.apple.screensaver askForPasswordDelay = <integer><0,5></integer>. Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/sysadminctl -screenLock immediate -password <administrator password> or ; sudo /usr/sbin/sysadminctl -screenLock 5 seconds -password <administrator password>. GUI: System Settings > Lock Screen > Set Require password after screensaver begins or display is turned off to either After 0 seconds or After 5 seconds.

title: Ensure Login Window Displays as Name and Password Is Enabled
description: The login window prompts a user for his/her credentials, verifies their authorization level, and then allows or denies the user access to the system.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.11.4 Ensure Login Window Displays as Name and Password Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.loginwindow').objectForKey('SHOWFULLNAME').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.loginwindow SHOWFULLNAME = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow SHOWFULLNAME -bool true. GUI: System Settings > Lock Screen > Set 'Login window shows' to Name and Password.

title: Ensure Show Password Hints Is Disabled
description: Password hints are user-created text displayed when an incorrect password is used for an account.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.11.5 Ensure Show Password Hints Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.loginwindow').objectForKey('RetriesUntilHint').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.loginwindow RetriesUntilHint = <integer>0</integer>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow RetriesUntilHint -int 0. GUI: System Settings > Lock Screen > Set 'Show password hints` to disabled.

title: Ensure Users' Accounts Do Not Have a Password Hint
description: Password hints help the user recall their passwords for various systems and/or accounts. In most cases, password hints are simple and closely related to the user's password. Audit: Counts users that have any password hint text.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.12.1 Ensure Users' Accounts Do Not Have a Password Hint

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users hint 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/awk 'NF > 1 {n++} END {print n+0}'

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users hint . -delete /Users/<username> hint ; sudo /usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users hint . -delete /Users/firstuser hint ; sudo /usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users hint . -delete /Users/seconduser hint. GUI: System Settings > Touch ID & Passwords (or Login Password on non-Touch ID Macs) > Change > Change the password and ensure that no text is entered in the Password hint box.

title: Ensure Guest Account Is Disabled
description: The guest account allows users access to the system without having to create an account or password. Guest users are unable to make setting changes and cannot remotely login to the system. All files, caches, and passwords created by the guest user are deleted upon logging out.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.13.1 Ensure Guest Account Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX DisableGuestAccount = <true/>; com.apple.MCX EnableGuestAccount = <false/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow GuestEnabled -bool false. GUI: System Settings > Users & Groups > i next to the Guest User > Set Allow guests to log in to this computer to disabled.

title: Ensure Guest Access to Shared Folders Is Disabled
description: Allowing guests to connect to shared folders enables users to access selected shared folders and their contents from different computers on a network.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.13.2 Ensure Guest Access to Shared Folders Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/sysadminctl -smbGuestAccess status 2>&1) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -q "SMB guest access disabled" && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/sysadminctl -smbGuestAccess off. GUI: System Settings > Users & Groups > i next to the Guest User > Set Allow guests to connect to shared folders to disabled.

title: Ensure Automatic Login Is Disabled
description: The automatic login feature saves a user's system access credentials and bypasses the login screen. Instead, the system automatically loads to the user's desktop screen.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.13.3 Ensure Automatic Login Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.loginwindow com.apple.login.mcx.DisableAutoLoginClient = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults delete /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUser. GUI: System Settings > Users & Groups > Set Automatic login in as... to Off.

title: Ensure Security Auditing Is Enabled
description: macOS's audit facility, auditd, receives notifications from the kernel when certain system calls, such as open, fork, and exit, are made. These notifications are captured and written to an audit log. Apple has deprecated auditd as of macOS 11.0 Big Sur. In macOS 14.0 Sonoma it is no longer enabled by default and it is suggested to use an application that integrates with the EndpointSecurity API.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.1 Ensure Security Auditing Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qi com.apple.auditd && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.auditd.plist ; sudo /bin/cp /etc/security/audit_control.example /etc/security/audit_control.

title: Ensure Access to Audit Records Is Controlled
description: The audit system on macOS writes important operational and security information that can be both useful for an attacker and a place for an attacker to attempt to obfuscate unwanted changes that were recorded. As part of defense-in-depth, the /etc/security/audit_control configuration and the files in /var/audit should be owned only by root with group wheel with read-only rights and no other access allowed. Audit: audit_control and the audit log directory must be owned by root:wheel (uid/gid 0) and mode -r--r-----.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.5 Ensure Access to Audit Records Is Controlled

audit.command:
f=/etc/security/audit_control
[ -e "$f" ] || exit 1
d=$(/usr/bin/grep '^dir' "$f" | /usr/bin/awk -F: '{print $2}')
[ -n "$d" ] && [ -d "$d" ] || exit 1
r1=$(/bin/ls -n "$f" | /usr/bin/awk '{s+=$3} END {print s+0}')
r2=$(/bin/ls -n "$f" | /usr/bin/awk '{s+=$4} END {print s+0}')
r3=$(/bin/ls -n "$f" | /usr/bin/awk '!/-r--r-----|current|total/{print $1}' | /usr/bin/wc -l | /usr/bin/tr -d ' ')
r4=$(/bin/ls -n "$d" | /usr/bin/awk '{s+=$3} END {print s+0}')
r5=$(/bin/ls -n "$d" | /usr/bin/awk '{s+=$4} END {print s+0}')
r6=$(/bin/ls -n "$d" | /usr/bin/awk '!/-r--r-----|current|total/{print $1}' | /usr/bin/wc -l | /usr/bin/tr -d ' ')
if [ "$r1$r2$r3$r4$r5$r6" = 000000 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "owner/group/mode checks: $r1 $r2 $r3 $r4 $r5 $r6"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/chown -R root:wheel /etc/security/audit_control ; sudo /bin/chmod -R 700 /etc/security/audit_control ; sudo /usr/sbin/chown -R root:wheel $(sudo /usr/bin/grep '^dir' /etc/security/audit_control | /usr/bin/awk -F: '{print $2}').

title: Ensure Home Folders Are Secure
description: By default, macOS allows all valid users into the top level of every other user's home folder and restricts access to the Apple default folders within. Another user on the same system can see you have a "Documents" folder but cannot see inside it. This configuration does work for personal file sharing but can expose user files to standard accounts on the system. Audit: Counts home folders under /System/Volumes/Data/Users not set to 700 (710/711 are accepted, per the benchmark alternative).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure Home Folders Are Secure

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/find /System/Volumes/Data/Users -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -not -perm 700 -not -perm 710 -not -perm 711 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -v "Shared" | /usr/bin/grep -v "Guest" | /usr/bin/grep -c . || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/chmod -R og-rwx /Users/<username> Alternately, run the following command if there needs to be executable access for a home folder: ; sudo /bin/chmod -R og-rw /Users/<username> ; sudo /bin/chmod -R og-rw /Users/firstuser/.

title: Ensure System Integrity Protection Status (SIP) Is Enabled
description: System Integrity Protection is a security feature introduced in OS X 10.11 El Capitan. System Integrity Protection restricts access to System domain locations and restricts runtime attachment to system processes. Any attempt to inspect or attach to a system process will fail. Kernel Extensions are now restricted to /Library/Extensions and are required to be signed with a Developer ID.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.2 Ensure System Integrity Protection Status (SIP) Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/csrutil status 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -q "System Integrity Protection status: enabled" && echo compliant

remediation.command: Boot into macOS Recovery (Apple silicon: hold the power button at startup; Intel: hold Command-R), open Utilities > Terminal and run /usr/bin/csrutil enable, then restart the Mac. SIP cannot be re-enabled from the running OS.

title: Ensure Apple Mobile File Integrity (AMFI) Is Enabled
description: Apple Mobile File Integrity (AMFI) was first released in macOS 10.12. The daemon and service block attempts to run unsigned code. AMFI uses launchd, code signatures, certificates, entitlements, and provisioning profiles to create a filtered entitlement dictionary for an app. AMFI is the macOS kernel module that enforces code-signing and library validation.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure Apple Mobile File Integrity (AMFI) Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/nvram -p 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c "amfi_get_out_of_my_way=1" || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/nvram boot-args="".

title: Ensure Signed System Volume (SSV) Is Enabled
description: Signed System Volume is a security feature introduced in macOS 11.0 Big Sur. During system installation, a SHA-256 cryptographic hash is calculated for all immutable system files and stored in a Merkle tree which itself is hashed as the Seal. Both are stored in the metadata of the snapshot created of the System volume. The seal is verified by the boot loader at startup.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.4 Ensure Signed System Volume (SSV) Is Enabled

audit.command: /usr/bin/csrutil authenticated-root status 2>/dev/null

remediation.command: If SSV has been disabled, assume that the operating system has been compromised. Back up any files, and do a clean install to a known good Operating System.

title: Ensure Appropriate Permissions Are Enabled for System Wide Applications
description: Applications in the System Applications Directory (/Applications) should be world- executable since that is their reason to be on the system. They should not be world- writable and allow any process or user to alter them for other processes or users to then execute modified versions. Some application vendors use a world-writable folder for their applications. This is against the standard practice on POSIX systems.

title: Ensure Password Age Is Configured
