title: Ensure Download New Updates When Available Is Enabled
description: In the GUI, both "Install macOS updates" and "Install app updates from the App Store" are dependent on whether "Download new updates when available" is selected.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.2 Ensure Download New Updates When Available Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.SoftwareUpdate').objectForKey('AutomaticDownload').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticDownload = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticDownload -bool true. GUI: System Settings > General > Software Update > i > Set Download new updates when available to enabled > Done.

title: Ensure Install of macOS Updates Is Enabled
description: Ensure that macOS updates are installed after they are available from Apple. This setting enables macOS updates to be automatically installed. Some environments will want to approve and test updates before they are delivered. It is best practice to test first where updates can and have caused disruptions to operations.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.3 Ensure Install of macOS Updates Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.SoftwareUpdate').objectForKey('AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates -bool TRUE. GUI: System Settings > General > Software Update > i > Set Install macOS updates to enabled > Done.

title: Ensure Install Application Updates from the App Store Is Enabled
description: Ensure that application updates are installed after they are available from Apple. These updates do not require reboots or administrator privileges for end users.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.4 Ensure Install Application Updates from the App Store Is Enabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticallyInstallAppUpdates = <true/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.commerce AutoUpdate -bool TRUE. GUI: System Settings > General > Software Update > i > Set Install application updates from the App Store to enabled > Done.

title: Ensure iCloud Drive Document and Desktop Sync Is Disabled
description: With macOS 10.12, Apple introduced the capability to have a user's Desktop and Documents folders automatically synchronize to the user's iCloud Drive, provided they have enough room purchased through Apple on their iCloud Drive. This capability mirrors what Microsoft is doing with the use of OneDrive and Office 365. There are concerns with using this capability.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.1.1.3 Ensure iCloud Drive Document and Desktop Sync Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowCloudDesktopAndDocuments').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowCloudDesktopAndDocuments = <false/>.

title: Ensure AirDrop Is Disabled When Not Actively Transferring Files
description: AirDrop is Apple's built-in, on-demand, ad hoc file exchange system that is compatible with both macOS and iOS. It uses Bluetooth LE for discovery that limits connectivity to Mac or iOS users that are in close proximity. Depending on the setting, it allows everyone or only Contacts to share files when they are near each other. In many ways, this technology is far superior to the alternatives.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.1.1 Ensure AirDrop Is Disabled When Not Actively Transferring Files

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowAirDrop').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowAirDrop = <false/>.

title: Ensure Set Time and Date Automatically Is Enabled
description: Correct date and time settings are required for authentication protocols, file creation, modification dates, and log entries. Note: If your organization has internal time servers, enter them here. Enterprise mobile devices may need to use a mix of internal and external time servers. If multiple servers are required, use the Date & Time System Preference with each server separated by a space.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.2.1 Ensure Set Time and Date Automatically Is Enabled

audit.command: /usr/sbin/systemsetup -getusingnetworktime 2>/dev/null

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setnetworktimeserver <your.time.server> ; sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setusingnetworktime on ; sudo /usr/sbin/systemsetup -setnetworktimeserver time.apple.com. GUI: System Settings > General > Date & Time > Set Set time and date automatically to enabled.

title: Ensure the Time Service Is Enabled
description: In macOS 10.14, Apple replace ntp with timed for time services, and is used to ensure correct time is kept. Correct date and time settings are required for authentication protocols, file creation, modification dates, and log entries.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.2.2 Ensure the Time Service Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c 'com.apple.timed' || true

remediation.guidance: If the timed service has been disabled, assume that the operating system has been compromised. Back up any files, and do a clean install to a known good Operating System.

title: Ensure Printer Sharing Is Disabled
description: By enabling Printer Sharing, the computer is set up as a print server to accept print jobs from other computers. Dedicated print servers or direct IP printing should be used instead.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.3 Ensure Printer Sharing Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/cupsctl 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c "_share_printers=0" || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/cupsctl --no-share-printers. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Printer Sharing to disabled.

title: Ensure Bluetooth Sharing Is Disabled
description: Bluetooth Sharing allows files to be exchanged with Bluetooth-enabled devices. This setting only disables the receiving of files and requires both devices to be paired through Bluetooth as well as accepted by the receiver. This setting does not disable the ability to send files from the device to another paired Bluetooth device. Audit: Checks PrefKeyServicesEnabled for every local user (UID > 500); an unset key is the off-by-default state.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.10 Ensure Bluetooth Sharing Is Disabled

audit.command:
ul=$(/usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users UniqueID 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=""
for u in $(printf '%s\n' "$ul" | /usr/bin/awk '$2 > 500 {print $1}'); do
  v=$(/usr/bin/sudo -u "$u" /usr/bin/defaults -currentHost read com.apple.Bluetooth PrefKeyServicesEnabled 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != 0 ] && bad="$bad $u"
done
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "Bluetooth Sharing enabled for:$bad"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults -currentHost write com.apple.Bluetooth PrefKeyServicesEnabled -bool false ; sudo -u firstuser /usr/bin/defaults -currentHost write com.apple.Bluetooth PrefKeyServicesEnabled -bool false. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Bluetooth Sharing to disabled.

title: Ensure Computer Name Does Not Contain PII or Protected Organizational Information
description: If the computer is used in an organization that assigns host names, it is a good idea to change the computer name to the host name. This is more of a best practice than a security measure. If the host name and the computer name are the same, computer support may be able to track problems down more easily.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.3.11 Ensure Computer Name Does Not Contain PII or Protected Organizational Information

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Verify that Hostname is set to your organization's parameters.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Edit > Set Hostname to your organization's parameters.

title: Ensure Backup Automatically is Enabled If Time Machine Is Enabled
description: Backup solutions are only effective if the backups run on a regular basis. The time to check for backups is before the hard drive fails or the computer goes missing. In order to simplify the user experience so that backups are more likely to occur, Time Machine should be on and set to Back Up Automatically whenever the target volume is available. Audit: Passes when Time Machine is not configured (preference not set) or AutoBackup is enabled.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.3.4.1 Ensure Backup Automatically is Enabled If Time Machine Is Enabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX.TimeMachine AutoBackup = <true/>. GUI: System Settings > General > Time Machine > Options > Set Back up frequency to Automatically <every hour/every day/every week>.

title: Ensure 'Share with app developers' Is Disabled
description: Share with app developers allows Apple to share crash and usage data with app developers. Turn off all Analytics and Improvements sharing.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.3.4 Ensure 'Share with app developers' Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowDiagnosticSubmission').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowDiagnosticSubmission = <false/>.

title: Ensure the OS Is Not Active When Resuming from Standby (Intel)
description: In order to use a computer with Full Disk Encryption (FDE), macOS must keep encryption keys in memory to allow the use of the disk that has been FileVault protected. The storage volume has been unlocked and acts as if it were not encrypted. When the system is not in use, the volume is protected through encryption.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.10.1.1 Ensure the OS Is Not Active When Resuming from Standby (Intel)

audit.command: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | /usr/bin/grep -e MacBook ; sudo /usr/bin/pmset -b -g | /usr/bin/grep -e standby If there is an output, run the following: % /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/pmset -b -g | /usr/bin/grep -e standby The output should include a standbydelaylow value ≤ 900, a standbydelayhigh value ≤ 900, and a highstandbythreshol

remediation.command: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a standbydelaylow <value≤900> ; sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a standbydelayhigh <value≤900> ; sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a highstandbythreshold <value≥90>.

title: Ensure Sleep and Display Sleep Is Enabled on Apple Silicon Devices
description: MacBooks should be set so that the sleep is 15 minutes or less and the display should sleep at 10 minutes or less. This setting should allow laptop users in most cases to stay within physically secured areas while going to a conference room, auditorium, or other internal location without having to unlock the encryption. Audit: Applies to Apple silicon MacBooks only (others report compliant): battery sleep <= 15 and displaysleep <= 10 and <= sleep.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.10.1.2 Ensure Sleep and Display Sleep Is Enabled on Apple Silicon Devices

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/sbin/ioreg ] || exit 1
m=$(/usr/sbin/ioreg -k product-name | /usr/bin/awk -F '"' '/product-name/ { if ( $0 ~ "MacBook" ) { print $4 } }')
[ -n "$m" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }
/usr/sbin/sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string | /usr/bin/grep -q Apple || { echo compliant; exit 0; }
s=$(/usr/bin/pmset -b -g | /usr/bin/awk '$1 == "sleep" {print $2}')
d=$(/usr/bin/pmset -b -g | /usr/bin/awk '$1 == "displaysleep" {print $2}')
if [ -n "$s" ] && [ -n "$d" ] && [ "$s" -le 15 ] && [ "$d" -le 10 ] && [ "$d" -le "$s" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "sleep=$s displaysleep=$d"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a sleep <value≤15> ; sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a displaysleep <value≤10 & < value of sleep> ; sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a sleep 15.

title: Ensure an Inactivity Interval of 15 Minutes Or Less for the Screen Saver Is Enabled
description: A locking screen saver is one of the standard security controls to limit access to a computer and the current user's session when the computer is temporarily unused or unattended. In macOS, the screen saver starts after a value is selected in the drop- down menu. 15 minutes or less is an acceptable value. Audit: Unlike the benchmark script, an unset idleTime fails (JavaScript treats null <= 900 as true).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.11.1 Ensure an Inactivity Interval of 15 Minutes Or Less for the Screen Saver Is Enabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.screensaver idleTime = <integer><≤900></integer>.

title: Ensure Security Auditing Flags For User-Attributable Events Are Configured Per Local Organizational Requirements
description: Auditing is the capture and maintenance of information about security-related events. Auditable events often depend on differing organizational requirements. Audit: Requires aa, ad, lo and -ex, -fm, -fr, -fw (or -all) in the flags line of /etc/security/audit_control.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.2 Ensure Security Auditing Flags For User-Attributable Events Are Configured Per Local Organizational Requirements

audit.command:
l=$(/usr/bin/grep -e "^flags:" /etc/security/audit_control 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
f=",$(printf '%s' "${l#flags:}" | /usr/bin/tr -d ' '),"
miss=""
for x in aa ad lo; do case "$f" in *",$x,"*) ;; *) miss="$miss $x";; esac; done
case "$f" in
  *",-all,"*|*",all,"*) ;;
  *) for x in ex fm fr fw; do case "$f" in *",-$x,"*|*",$x,"*) ;; *) miss="$miss -$x";; esac; done;;
esac
if [ -z "$miss" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "missing flags:$miss"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: Edit the /etc/security/audit_control file and add aa, ad, -ex, -fm, -fr, -fw, and lo to flags. You can also substitute -all for -ex, -fm, -fr, and -fw.

title: Ensure install.log Is Retained for 365 or More Days and No Maximum Size
description: macOS writes information pertaining to system-related events to the file /var/log/install.log and has a configurable retention policy for this file. The default logging setting limits the file size of the logs and the maximum size for all logs. The default allows for an errant application to fill the log files and does not enforce sufficient log retention. Audit: Requires ttl >= 365 and no all_max= setting in /etc/asl/com.apple.install.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.3 Ensure install.log Is Retained for 365 or More Days and No Maximum Size

audit.command:
f=/etc/asl/com.apple.install
[ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
t=$(/usr/bin/grep -io 'ttl=[0-9]*' "$f" | /usr/bin/head -1 | /usr/bin/cut -d= -f2)
if [ -n "$t" ] && [ "$t" -ge 365 ] && ! /usr/bin/grep -qi 'all_max=' "$f"; then echo compliant; else echo "ttl=${t:-unset}; all_max present or ttl < 365"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: Edit the /etc/asl/com.apple.install file and add or modify the ttl value to 365 or greater on the file line. Also, remove the all_max= setting and value from the file line.

title: Ensure Security Auditing Logs Are Retained for 30 Days
description: The macOS audit capability contains important information to investigate security or operational issues. This resource is only completely useful if it is retained long enough to allow technical staff to find the root cause of anomalies in the records. Retention can be set to respect both size and longevity. Audit: Requires a day-based expire-after value of at least 30d.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.4 Ensure Security Auditing Logs Are Retained for 30 Days

audit.command:
l=$(/usr/bin/grep -e "^expire-after" /etc/security/audit_control 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
d=$(printf '%s' "$l" | /usr/bin/grep -oE '[0-9]+d' | /usr/bin/head -1 | /usr/bin/tr -d d)
if [ -n "$d" ] && [ "$d" -ge 30 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "$l"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: Edit the /etc/security/audit_control file so that expire-after: is at least 30d

title: Ensure HTTP Server Is Disabled
description: macOS used to have a graphical front-end to the embedded Apache web server in the operating system. Personal web sharing could be enabled to allow someone on another computer to download files or information from the user's computer. Personal web sharing from a user endpoint has long been considered questionable, and Apple has removed that capability from the GUI.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2 Ensure HTTP Server Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c 'org.apache.httpd' || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/apachectl stop ; sudo /bin/launchctl unload -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/org.apache.httpd.plist.

title: Ensure NFS Server Is Disabled
description: macOS can act as an NFS fileserver. NFS sharing could be enabled to allow someone on another computer to mount shares and gain access to information from the user's computer. File sharing from a user endpoint has long been considered questionable, and Apple has removed that capability from the GUI.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.3 Ensure NFS Server Is Disabled

audit.command:
s=$(/sbin/nfsd status 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk '/nfsd service/ { print $NF }') || exit 1
if [ "$s" = disabled ] && [ ! -e /etc/exports ]; then echo compliant; else echo "nfsd=${s:-unknown}; /etc/exports present or service enabled"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl disable system/com.apple.nfsd ; sudo /bin/rm -rf /etc/exports.

title: Ensure a Separate Timestamp Is Enabled for Each User/tty Combo
description: Using tty tickets ensures that a user must enter the sudo password in each Terminal session. With sudo versions 1.8 and higher, introduced in 10.12, the default value is to have tty tickets for each interface so that root access is limited to a specific terminal. The default configuration can be overwritten or not configured correctly on earlier versions of macOS.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.5 Ensure a Separate Timestamp Is Enabled for Each User/tty Combo

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/sudo -V 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -c "Type of authentication timestamp record: tty" || true

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/<configuration file name>.

title: Ensure a Login Window Banner Exists
description: A Login window banner warning informs the user that the system is reserved for authorized use only. It enforces an acknowledgment by the user that they have been informed of the use policy in the banner if required. The system recognizes either the .txt and the .rtf formats. Audit: A /Library/Security/PolicyBanner.* file must exist and its mode must have 4 as the third digit.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.8 Ensure a Login Window Banner Exists

audit.command:
set -- /Library/Security/PolicyBanner.*
[ -e "$1" ] || exit 1
for f in "$@"; do
  p=$(/usr/bin/stat -f %A "$f") || exit 1
  case "$p" in ??4) ;; *) echo "$f mode $p"; exit 0;; esac
done
echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/chmod o+r /Library/Security/PolicyBanner.txt ; sudo /bin/chmod o+r /Library/Security/PolicyBanner.rtf.

title: Ensure Protect Mail Activity in Mail Is Enabled
description: Apple provides privacy protection that should be enabled for the mail app on macOS to reduce information collection from a user that receives email.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.2.1 Ensure Protect Mail Activity in Mail Is Enabled

audit.command: GUI: Mail > Mail in the menu bar > Settings > Privacy > Verify that Protect Mail Activity is enabled.

remediation.command: GUI: Mail > Mail in the menu bar > Settings > Privacy > Set Protect Mail Activity to enabled.

title: Ensure Automatic Opening of Safe Files in Safari Is Disabled
description: Safari will automatically run or execute what it considers safe files. This can include installers and other files that execute on the operating system. Safari evaluates file safety by using a list of filetypes maintained by Apple. The list of files include text, image, video and archive formats that would be run in the context of the OS rather than the browser.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.1 Ensure Automatic Opening of Safe Files in Safari Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -E 'AutoOpenSafeDownloads' | /usr/bin/tr -d ' '

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari AutoOpenSafeDownloads = <false/>.

title: Ensure Warn When Visiting A Fraudulent Website in Safari Is Enabled
description: Apple uses the Google Safe Browsing API to check for fraudulent websites and report them to the user attempting to visit one.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.3 Ensure Warn When Visiting A Fraudulent Website in Safari Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -E 'WarnAboutFraudulentWebsites' | /usr/bin/tr -d ' '

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari WarnAboutFraudulentWebsites = <true/>.

title: Ensure Secure Keyboard Entry Terminal.app Is Enabled
description: Secure Keyboard Entry prevents other applications on the system and/or network from detecting and recording what is typed into Terminal. Unauthorized applications and malicious code could intercept keystrokes entered in the Terminal.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.4.1 Ensure Secure Keyboard Entry Terminal.app Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.Terminal').objectForKey('SecureKeyboardEntry').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Terminal SecureKeyboardEntry = <true/>.

title: Audit iCloud Passwords & Keychain
description: The iCloud Passwords & Keychain is Apple's synchronization service that works with Apple Accounts to synchronize password, passkey, and credit card information across macOS, iOS, iPadOS. The capability allows users to use synced password, passkey, and credit card information in either macOS, iOS, or iPadOS for use in Safari and other applications.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1.1 Audit iCloud Passwords & Keychain

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Disallow iCloud Keychain Sync set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key allowCloudKeychainSync If the output is false, iCloud Passwords & Keychain Sync is disabled. If the output is true, iCloud Passwords & Keychain sync is enabled.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowCloudKeychainSync.

title: Audit iCloud Drive
description: iCloud Drive is Apple's storage solution for applications on both macOS and iOS to use the same files that are resident in Apple's cloud storage. The iCloud Drive folder is available much like Dropbox, Microsoft OneDrive, or Google Drive. One of the concerns in public cloud storage is that proprietary data may be inappropriately stored in an end user's personal repository.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1.2 Audit iCloud Drive

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Disallow iCloud Drive set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key allowCloudDocumentSync If the output is false, iCloud Drive Sync is disabled. If the output is true, iCloud Drive sync is enabled.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowCloudDocumentSync.

title: Audit Security Keys Used With Apple Accounts
description: Apple has introduced the capability of using security keys to protect Apple Accounts using two-factor authentication in macOS 13.2, in iOS 16.3, and in iPadOS 16.3. This feature along with the purchase of two hardware tokens (a backup device is required) protects against the compromise of Apple Accounts. This feature requires all devices using an enrolled Apple Account to meet the minimum OS standard.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1.4 Audit Security Keys Used With Apple Accounts

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > Password & Security > Verify that Security Keys is set to your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > Password & Security > Add.. to add a security key, or Remove All Security Keys ro remove security keys, to meet your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Freeform Sync to iCloud
description: Starting with macOS 13.1 Apple has made FreeForm, a collaboration tool, available for macOS, iOS and iPadOS. This application allows for extensive whiteboard creation and sharing using iCloud. Organizations may want to audit the use of Freeform iCloud sharing of internally created boards.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1.5 Audit Freeform Sync to iCloud

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Disallow iCloud Freeform Sync set to your organization's requirement. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key allowCloudFreeform The output should match your organization's requirement

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowCloudFreeform = <<true/false>/>.

title: Audit Find My Mac
description: Find My is Apple's consumer solution for device tracking of your devices. This allows a user to track the location of devices associated with their Apple Account. This is a great solution for consumer or user device management and tracking, but it is not meant to be an enterprise management solution to device tracking and information management on enterprise managed devices.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.1.6 Audit Find My Mac

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > iCloud > Show More Apps > Verify that Find My Mac is set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key allowFindMyDevice The output will either be true, Find My Device is enabled, or false, Find My Device is disabled depending on your organizations requirements.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowFindMyDevice = <<true/>or<false/>> depending on your organization's. GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > iCloud > Show More Apps > Set Find My Mac is set to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit App Store Password Settings
description: With Mac OS X 10.11, Apple added settings for password storage for the App Store in macOS. These settings parallel the settings in iOS. As with iOS, the choices are a requirement to provide a password after every purchase or to have a 15-minute grace period, and whether or not to require a password for free purchases. The response to this setting is stored in a cookie and processed by iCloud.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.2 Audit App Store Password Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > Media & Purchases > Verify that Free Downloads is set to your organization's requirements > Verify that Purchases and In-App Purchases is set to your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Apple Account > Media & Purchases > Set Free Downloads to your organization's requirements > Set Purchases and In-App Purchases to your organization's requirements.

title: Ensure AirPlay Receiver Is Disabled
description: In macOS Monterey (12.0), Apple has added the capability to share content from another Apple device to the screen of a host Mac. While there are many valuable uses of this capability, such sharing on a standard Mac user workstation should be enabled ad hoc as required rather than allowing a continuous sharing service.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3.1.2 Ensure AirPlay Receiver Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowAirPlayIncomingRequests').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowAirPlayIncomingRequests = <false/>.

title: Ensure Content Caching Is Disabled
description: Starting with macOS 10.13, Apple introduced a service to make it easier to deploy data from Apple, including software updates, where there are bandwidth constraints to the Internet and fewer constraints or greater bandwidth exist on the local subnet. This capability can be very valuable for organizations that have throttled and possibly metered Internet connections.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3.3.8 Ensure Content Caching Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowContentCaching = <false/>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/AssetCacheManagerUtil deactivate. GUI: System Settings > General > Sharing > Set Content Caching to disabled.

title: Ensure Media Sharing Is Disabled
description: Starting with macOS 10.15, Apple has provided a control which permits a user to share Apple downloaded content on all Apple devices that are signed in with the same Apple Account. This allows users to share downloaded Movies, Music, or TV shows with other controlled macOS, iOS and iPadOS devices, as well as photos with Apple TVs. With this capability, guest users can also use media downloaded on the computer.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3.3.9 Ensure Media Sharing Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowMediaSharing = <false/>; com.apple.applicationaccess allowMediaSharingModification = <false/>.

title: Audit Menu Bar and Control Center Icons
description: The Menu Bar is the horizontal strip that runs across the very top of your Mac's screen. The Control Center is a panel that groups the most frequently used system settings into one convenient location, similar to Control Center on an iPhone or iPad.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4.1 Audit Menu Bar and Control Center Icons

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Menu Bar > Verify that all items listed in the Allow in the menu bar section are allowed by your organization > Control Center icon in the menu bar > Verify that the Control Center options meet your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Menu Bar > Remove any items in Allow in the menu bar section are not allowed by your organization. Control Center icon in the menu bar > Set the Control Center options to meet your organization's requirements.

title: Ensure External Intelligence Extensions Is Disabled
description: The External Intelligence Extensions allows Apple Intelligence to interface with third-party generative AI tools. Apple's external intelligence extension represents a calculated risk. Audit: Both allowExternalIntelligenceIntegrations and allowExternalIntelligenceIntegrationsSignIn must be false.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.1.1 Ensure External Intelligence Extensions Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowExternalIntelligenceIntegrations = <false/>; com.apple.applicationaccess allowExternalIntelligenceIntegrationsSignIn = <false/>.

title: Ensure Writing Tools Is Disabled
description: Apple Intelligence Writing Tools are a suite of AI-powered features integrated across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, enabling users to enhance their text by proofreading for errors, rewriting content to adjust tone or style, summarizing lengthy passages into concise forms, and even composing new text from scratch.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.1.2 Ensure Writing Tools Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowWritingTools').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowWritingTools = <false/>.

title: Ensure Mail Summarization Is Disabled
description: Apple Intelligence's Mail summarization feature uses AI to quickly condense long emails or entire email threads into a few key sentences or bullet points.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.1.3 Ensure Mail Summarization Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowMailSummary').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowMailSummary = <false/>.

title: Ensure Notes Summarization Is Disabled
description: Apple Intelligence's Notes summarization feature quickly condenses content within the Notes app. This includes summarizing written text you've highlighted or, notably, automatically generating summaries from audio recordings taken directly within Notes, like lectures or meetings, helping you grasp key information at a glance. Audit: Both allowNotesTranscription and allowNotesTranscriptionSummary must be false.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.1.4 Ensure Notes Summarization Is Disabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowNotesTranscription = <false/>; com.apple.applicationaccess allowNotesTranscriptionSummary = <false/>.

title: Ensure Siri Is Disabled
description: With macOS 10.12 Sierra, Apple has introduced Siri from iOS to macOS. While there are data spillage concerns with the use of data-gathering personal assistant software, the risk here does not seem greater in sending queries to Apple through Siri than in sending search terms in a browser to Google or Microsoft.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.2.1 Ensure Siri Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowAssistant').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowAssistant.

title: Ensure Listen for (Siri) Is Disabled
description: macOS includes the Siri digital assistant and if enabled it is always listening in case it is needed. In Sonoma a user may choose either "Hey Siri" or either "Siri" and "Hey Siri." In either case, Siri is using the microphone at all times to listen for instructions and then can record questions once activated.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.2.2 Ensure Listen for (Siri) Is Disabled

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has VoiceTriggerUserEnabled set to 0. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.Siri, key VoiceTriggerUserEnabled

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Siri set to VoiceTriggerUserEnabled = <false/>.

title: Ensure Location Services Is Enabled
description: macOS uses location information gathered through local Wi-Fi networks to enable applications to supply relevant information to users. With the operating system verifying the location, users do not need to change the time or the time zone. The computer will change them based on the user's location.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.6.1.1 Ensure Location Services Is Enabled

audit.command:
n=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c com.apple.locationd)
e=$(/usr/bin/sudo -u _locationd /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.locationd').objectForKey('LocationServicesEnabled').js
EOS
) || exit 1
if [ "${n:-0}" -ge 1 ] && [ "$e" = true ]; then echo compliant; else echo "locationd=$n LocationServicesEnabled=${e:-unset}"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.locationd.plist ; sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /var/db/locationd/Library/Preferences/ByHost/com.apple.locationd LocationServicesEnabled -bool true ; sudo /usr/bin/killall locationd. GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Set Location Services to enabled.

While Location Services may be very useful, it may not be desirable to allow all applications that can use Location Services to use your location for Internet queries in order to provide tailored content based on your current location.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.6.1.3 Audit Location Services Access

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Verify that the applications allowed to access Location Services are set to your organization's requirements Perform the following steps to verify what websites are enabled to ask for access to. Location Services: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Websites > Location > Verify that When visiting other websites is set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults read /var/db/locationd/clients.plist Ensure that all applications listed have been authorized to access location information.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Set any applications listed to your organization's requirements Perform the following steps to set websites to ask for permission to access Location. title: Audit Full Disk Access for Applications
description: Starting with macOS 10.14 Mojave, Apple introduced Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) to enhance user privacy by requiring apps to get explicit permission before accessing sensitive data or system features. Full Disk Access (FDA) is a privacy category managed by the TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) framework.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.6.2.1 Audit Full Disk Access for Applications

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > Verify that the applications are set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/sqlite3 /Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db 'select client from access where auth_value and service = "kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles"' The output will be what applications have full disk access enabled.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > Set any listed applications to your organization's requirements > (Optional) Select the + to add applications to the list, or - to remove them.

Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults read .GlobalPreferences.plist LDMGlobalEnabled 2>/dev/null When Lockdown mode has been enabled, it will return 1 and when disabled return 0. If

title: Ensure Screen Saver Hot Corners Are Secure For Current User
description: Hot Corners can be configured to disable the screen saver by moving the mouse cursor to a corner of the screen. This can only be accomplished by the current user, so that is the only user that needs to be audited. Audit: Checks the console user (or loginwindow lastUserName); no corner may be set to 6 (Disable Screen Saver).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.7.1 Ensure Screen Saver Hot Corners Are Secure For Current User

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/defaults ] || exit 1
u=$(/usr/bin/stat -f%Su /dev/console 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != root ] || u=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow lastUserName 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=""
for c in bl tl tr br; do
  v=$(/usr/bin/defaults read "/Users/$u/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock" "wvous-$c-corner" 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$v" = 6 ] && bad="$bad $c"
done
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "hot corner set to disable screen saver:$bad"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-bl-corner 2>/dev/null ; sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-tl-corner 2>/dev/null ; sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-tr-corner 2>/dev/null. GUI: System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Hot Corners > Set and hot corner that is set to Disable Screen Saver to a setting that matches your organizational requirements.

title: Audit iPhone Mirroring
description: iPhone Mirroring is a new feature offered in iOS 18 and macOS 15.0 Sequoia. It allows a macOS device to remotely access an iOS device connected to the same Apple Account. If a user has different Apple Accounts signed into iOS and macOS (ex. a managed Apple Account on macOS and a personal Apple Account on iOS), the feature is not available.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.7.2 Audit iPhone Mirroring

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Allow iPhone Mirroring set to True or False based on your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple. applicationaccess, key allowiPhoneMirroring The output will be either true, allow iPhone mirroring, or false, disable iPhone mirroring.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowiPhoneMirroring = either <true/> or <false/> depending on your. GUI: System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Under the Widgets sub-header, verify iPhone is configured to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Universal Control Settings
description: Universal Control is an Apple feature that allows Mac users to control multiple other Macs and iPads with the same keyboard, mouse, and trackpad using the same Apple Account. The technology relies on already available iCloud services, particularly Handoff. Universal Control simplifies the use of iCloud connectivity of multiple computers using the same Apple Account.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.8.1 Audit Universal Control Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has with com.apple.universalcontrol in Settings and has Disable set to your organization's parameters. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.universalcontrol, key Disable If the output is true, Universal Control is disabled. If it is false, then Universal Control is enabled.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.universalcontrol Disable; com.apple.coreservices.useractivityd ClipboardSharingEnabled.

EOS

title: Ensure Power Nap Is Disabled for Intel Macs
description: Power Nap allows the system to stay in low power mode, especially while on battery power, and periodically connect to previously known networks with stored credentials for user applications to phone home and get updates. This capability requires FileVault to remain unlocked and the use of previously joined networks to be risk accepted based on the SSID without user input. Audit: Intel Macs only; Apple silicon reports 0 (not applicable).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.10.2 Ensure Power Nap Is Disabled for Intel Macs

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a powernap 0. GUI: Desktop Instructions: System Settings > Energy Saver > Set Power Nap to disabled > UPS (if applicable) > Set Power Nap to disabled. Laptop Instructions: System Settings > Battery > Power Adapter (for laptops only) > Set Power Nap to disabled > Battery > Set Power Nap to disabled > UPS (if applicable) > Set Power Nap to disabled.

title: Ensure Wake for Network Access Is Disabled
description: This feature allows the computer to take action when the user is not present and the computer is in energy saving mode. These tools require FileVault to remain unlocked and fully rejoin known networks. This macOS feature is meant to allow the computer to resume activity as needed regardless of physical security controls.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 26 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.10.3 Ensure Wake for Network Access Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/pmset -g custom 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/awk '$1 == "womp" && $2 != 0 {n++} END {print n+0}')
p=$(/usr/bin/profiles -P -o stdout 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c '"Wake On LAN" = 1')
if [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && [ "${p:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "womp enabled ($n) / profile Wake On LAN=1 ($p)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.desktop.ACPower = <dict>; com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.portable.ACPower = <dict>; com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.portable.BatteryPower = <dict>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a womp 0. GUI: Desktop Instructions: System Settings > Energy Saver > Set Wake for network access to disabled. Laptop Instructions: System Settings > Battery > Options > Set Wake for network access to Never.

title: Ensure a Custom Message for the Login Screen Is Enabled

title: Audit Touch ID

All use of Touch ID requires the presence of a password and the use of that password after every reboot, or when more than 48 hours has elapsed since the device was last unlocked. Touch ID is not a password replacement.

title: Audit Game Center Settings
description: With macOS 10.13, Apple has introduced a separate section for Game Center in System Settings. It is possible to log in with the Apple ID and use the iCloud-based Game Center services. Game Center is a feature from Apple that allows users to engage in game-related activities with friends when playing multiplayer games online on the Game Center social network.

If the output is true Game Center is enabled.

The tracking cookies allow information brokers to track web users across visited sites. if printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qx 'BlockStoragePolicy=2;' && printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qxF 'WebKitPreferences.storageBlockingPolicy=1;' && printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qx 'WebKitStorageBlockingPolicy=1;'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

(see benchmark)
