Select Settings 4. Select Privacy 5. Set Hide IP address from trackers to your organization's requirements Terminal Method: Run the following command to enable or disable hiding IP addresses from trackers in Safari: % /usr/bin/sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults write /Users/<username>/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Preference s/com.apple.Safari WBSPrivacyProxyAvailabilityTraffic -int <130272/130276> 33422560 will set hide IP address from trackers to disabled. 33422564 will enable from Trackers Only, and 33422572 will enabled from Trackers and Websites. example: % /usr/bin/sudo -u firstuser /usr/bin/defaults write /Users/firstuser/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Preferences /com.apple.Safari WBSPrivacyProxyAvailabilityTraffic -int 33422560 % /usr/bin/sudo -u seconduser /usr/bin/defaults write /Users/seconduser/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Preference s/com.apple.Safari WBSPrivacyProxyAvailabilityTraffic -int 33422564 % /usr/bin/sudo -u thirduser /usr/bin/defaults...

title: Ensure Advertising Privacy Protection in Safari Is Enabled
description: Apple provides a framework that allows advertisers to target Apple users and end-users with advertisements. While many people prefer that when they see advertising it is relevant to them and their interests, the detailed information that is data mining collected, correlated, and available to advertisers in repositories is often disconcerting. This information is valuable to both advertisers and attackers and has been used with other metadata to reveal users' identities. Organizations should manage advertising settings on computers rather than allow users to configure the settings. Apple Information Ad tracking should be limited on 10.15 and prior. Organizations should manage user privacy settings on managed devices to align with organizational policies and user data protection requirements.

In order to reduce the risk in interacting with unwanted content, the full website address should always be displayed in Safari. Full visibility into what site is being visited is important for privacy and security.

description: AutoFill capabilities in a Web Browser are a feature to allow a user to avoid re-typing the same user information in every form that a user encounters. Part of the modern internet consists of vendors establishing a seemingly close relationship with as many users as possible to market to them, data-mine from them and sell their data to third- party data aggregators. AutoFill can be a method for a user to share too much information with untrusted website owners. Many security professionals advise disabling AutoFill to reduce the risk of over-sharing. These security professionals appear to believe that manual data entry is better, since completing the required forms are often the only method to connect to needed data. The best method for security is to ensure that the data ready to be auto-filled is an acceptable risk to sites a user interacts with. Users must review what data they accep...

description: Browser pop-up windows have long been one of the most annoying delivery mechanisms of unwanted web content. The content can be unwanted content, including Not Safe For Work, or malicious content relying on a user interacting with the pop-up. Safari has a built-in capability to disable pop-ups that should be enabled. Pop-up windows are almost always unwanted content and should be blocked.

title: Audit iCloud Passwords & Keychain
description: The iCloud Passwords & Keychain is Apple's synchronization service that works with Apple Accounts to synchronize password, passkey, and credit card information across macOS, iOS, iPadOS. The capability allows users to use synced password, passkey, and credit card information in either macOS, iOS, or iPadOS for use in Safari and other applications.

The iCloud Drive folder is available much like Dropbox, Microsoft OneDrive, or Google Drive. One of the concerns in public cloud storage is that proprietary data may be inappropriately stored in an end user's personal repository.

title: Ensure Siri Is Disabled
description: With macOS 10.12 Sierra, Apple has introduced Siri from iOS to macOS. While there are data spillage concerns with the use of data-gathering personal assistant software, the risk here does not seem greater in sending queries to Apple through Siri than in sending search terms in a browser to Google or Microsoft.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.5.2.1 Ensure Siri Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowAssistant').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowAssistant.

title: Ensure Listen for (Siri) Is Disabled
description: macOS includes the Siri digital assistant and if enabled it is always listening in case it is needed. In Sonoma a user may choose either "Hey Siri" or either "Siri" and "Hey Siri." In either case, Siri is using the microphone at all times to listen for instructions and then can record questions once activated.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.5.2.2 Ensure Listen for (Siri) Is Disabled

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has VoiceTriggerUserEnabled set to 0. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.Siri, key VoiceTriggerUserEnabled

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Siri set to VoiceTriggerUserEnabled = <false/>.

title: Ensure Location Services Is Enabled
description: macOS uses location information gathered through local Wi-Fi networks to enable applications to supply relevant information to users. With the operating system verifying the location, users do not need to change the time or the time zone. The computer will change them based on the user's location.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.1.1 Ensure Location Services Is Enabled

audit.command:
n=$(/bin/launchctl list 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c com.apple.locationd)
e=$(/usr/bin/sudo -u _locationd /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.locationd').objectForKey('LocationServicesEnabled').js
EOS
) || exit 1
if [ "${n:-0}" -ge 1 ] && [ "$e" = true ]; then echo compliant; else echo "locationd=$n LocationServicesEnabled=${e:-unset}"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /bin/launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.locationd.plist ; sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /var/db/locationd/Library/Preferences/ByHost/com.apple.locationd LocationServicesEnabled -bool true ; sudo /usr/bin/killall locationd. GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Set Location Services to enabled.

title: Ensure 'Show Location Icon in Control Center when System Services Request Your Location' Is Enabled
description: This setting provides the user an understanding of the current status of Location Services and which applications are using it.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.1.2 Ensure 'Show Location Icon in Control Center when System Services Request Your Location' Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.locationmenu').objectForKey('ShowSystemServices').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.locationmenu.plist ShowSystemServices -bool true. GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Details > Set Show location icon in menu bar when System Services request your location to enabled.

title: Audit Location Services Access
description: macOS uses location information gathered through local Wi-Fi networks to enable applications to supply relevant information to users. While Location Services may be very useful, it may not be desirable to allow all applications that can use Location Services to use your location for Internet queries in order to provide tailored content based on your current location.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.1.3 Audit Location Services Access

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Verify that the applications allowed to access Location Services are set to your organization's requirements Perform the following steps to verify what websites are enabled to ask for access to. Location Services: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Websites > Location > Verify that When visiting other websites is set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults read /var/db/locationd/clients.plist Ensure that all applications listed have been authorized to access location information.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Set any applications listed to your organization's requirements Perform the following steps to set websites to ask for permission to access Location. Services: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Websites > Location > Set When visiting other websites to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Full Disk Access for Applications
description: Starting with macOS 10.14 Mojave, Apple introduced Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) to enhance user privacy by requiring apps to get explicit permission before accessing sensitive data or system features. Full Disk Access (FDA) is a privacy category managed by the TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) framework.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.2.1 Audit Full Disk Access for Applications

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > Verify that the applications are set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/sqlite3 /Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db 'select client from access where auth_value and service = "kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles"' The output will be what applications have full disk access enabled.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > Set any listed applications to your organization's requirements > (Optional) Select the + to add applications to the list, or - to remove them.

description: Apple provides a framework that allows advertisers to target Apple users and end-users with advertisements. While many people prefer to see advertising that is relevant to them and their interests, the detailed information that is collected, correlated, and available to advertisers in repositories via data mining is often disconcerting.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.4 Ensure Limit Ad Tracking Is Enabled

$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('allowApplePersonalizedAdvertising').js
EOS

title: Audit Lockdown Mode
description: Apple introduced Lockdown Mode as a security feature in their 2022 OS releases that provides additional security protection Apple describes as extreme. Users and organizations that suspect some users are targets of advanced attacks must consider using this control. When lockdown mode is enabled, specific trusted websites can be excluded from Lockdown protection if necessary.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.6.7 Audit Lockdown Mode

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Verify Lockdown Mode is set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults read .GlobalPreferences.plist LDMGlobalEnabled 2>/dev/null When Lockdown mode has been enabled, it will return 1 and when disabled return 0. If

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Set Lockdown Mode to your organization's requirements.

title: Ensure Screen Saver Hot Corners Are Secure For Current User
description: Hot Corners can be configured to disable the screen saver by moving the mouse cursor to a corner of the screen. This can only be accomplished by the current user, so that is the only user that needs to be audited. Audit: Checks the console user (or loginwindow lastUserName); no corner may be set to 6 (Disable Screen Saver).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.7.1 Ensure Screen Saver Hot Corners Are Secure For Current User

audit.command:
[ -x /usr/bin/defaults ] || exit 1
u=$(/usr/bin/stat -f%Su /dev/console 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != root ] || u=$(/usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow lastUserName 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=""
for c in bl tl tr br; do
  v=$(/usr/bin/defaults read "/Users/$u/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock" "wvous-$c-corner" 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$v" = 6 ] && bad="$bad $c"
done
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "hot corner set to disable screen saver:$bad"; fi

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-bl-corner 2>/dev/null ; sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-tl-corner 2>/dev/null ; sudo -u <current user> /usr/bin/defaults delete /Users/<current user>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock wvous-tr-corner 2>/dev/null. GUI: System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Hot Corners > Set and hot corner that is set to Disable Screen Saver to a setting that matches your organizational requirements.

title: Audit iPhone Mirroring
description: iPhone Mirroring is a new feature offered in iOS 18 and macOS 15.0 Sequoia. It allows a macOS device to remotely access an iOS device connected to the same Apple Account. If a user has different Apple Accounts signed into iOS and macOS (ex. a managed Apple Account on macOS and a personal Apple Account on iOS), the feature is not available.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.7.2 Audit iPhone Mirroring

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Allow iPhone Mirroring set to True or False based on your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple. applicationaccess, key allowiPhoneMirroring The output will be either true, allow iPhone mirroring, or false, disable iPhone mirroring.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowiPhoneMirroring = either <true/> or <false/> depending on your. GUI: System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Under the Widgets sub-header, verify iPhone is configured to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Universal Control Settings
description: Universal Control is an Apple feature that allows Mac users to control multiple other Macs and iPads with the same keyboard, mouse, and trackpad using the same Apple Account. The technology relies on already available iCloud services, particularly Handoff. Universal Control simplifies the use of iCloud connectivity of multiple computers using the same Apple Account.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.8.1 Audit Universal Control Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has with com.apple.universalcontrol in Settings and has Disable set to your organization's parameters. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.universalcontrol, key Disable If the output is true, Universal Control is disabled. If it is false, then Universal Control is enabled.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.universalcontrol Disable; com.apple.coreservices.useractivityd ClipboardSharingEnabled.

title: Ensure Help Apple Improve Search Is Disabled
description: Apple provides a mechanism to send diagnostic and analytics data back to Apple to help them improve the platform. Information sent to Apple may contain internal organizational information that should be controlled and not available for processing by Apple.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.9.1 Ensure Help Apple Improve Search Is Disabled

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Search Queries Data Sharing Status set to 2. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.assistant.support, key Search Queries Data Sharing Status

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.assistant.support set to Search Queries Data Sharing Status = <integer>2</integer>.

title: Ensure Power Nap Is Disabled for Intel Macs
description: Power Nap allows the system to stay in low power mode, especially while on battery power, and periodically connect to previously known networks with stored credentials for user applications to phone home and get updates. This capability requires FileVault to remain unlocked and the use of previously joined networks to be risk accepted based on the SSID without user input. Audit: Intel Macs only; Apple silicon reports 0 (not applicable).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.10.2 Ensure Power Nap Is Disabled for Intel Macs

remediation.guidance: Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a powernap 0. GUI: Desktop Instructions: System Settings > Energy Saver > Set Power Nap to disabled > UPS (if applicable) > Set Power Nap to disabled. Laptop Instructions: System Settings > Battery > Power Adapter (for laptops only) > Set Power Nap to disabled > Battery > Set Power Nap to disabled > UPS (if applicable) > Set Power Nap to disabled.

title: Ensure Wake for Network Access Is Disabled
description: This feature allows the computer to take action when the user is not present and the computer is in energy saving mode. These tools require FileVault to remain unlocked and fully rejoin known networks. This macOS feature is meant to allow the computer to resume activity as needed regardless of physical security controls.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.10.3 Ensure Wake for Network Access Is Disabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/bin/pmset -g custom 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/awk '$1 == "womp" && $2 != 0 {n++} END {print n+0}')
p=$(/usr/bin/profiles -P -o stdout 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c '"Wake On LAN" = 1')
if [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && [ "${p:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "womp enabled ($n) / profile Wake On LAN=1 ($p)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.desktop.ACPower = <dict>; com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.portable.ACPower = <dict>; com.apple.MCX com.apple.EnergySaver.portable.BatteryPower = <dict>. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/pmset -a womp 0. GUI: Desktop Instructions: System Settings > Energy Saver > Set Wake for network access to disabled. Laptop Instructions: System Settings > Battery > Options > Set Wake for network access to Never.

title: Ensure a Custom Message for the Login Screen Is Enabled
description: An access warning informs the user that the system is reserved for authorized use only, and that the use of the system may be monitored. Audit: Verify the text itself matches the organisation-approved message.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.11.3 Ensure a Custom Message for the Login Screen Is Enabled

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.loginwindow LoginwindowText = <string><Your organization's required. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow LoginwindowText "<custom message>" ; sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow LoginwindowText "Center for Internet Security Test Message". GUI: System Settings > Lock Screen > Set Show message when locked to enabled > Set > Insert text in the Set a message to appear on the lock screen that matches your organization's required text > Done.

title: Audit Touch ID
description: Apple has integrated Touch ID with macOS and allows fingerprint use for many common operations. All use of Touch ID requires the presence of a password and the use of that password after every reboot, or when more than 48 hours has elapsed since the device was last unlocked. Touch ID is not a password replacement.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.12.2 Audit Touch ID

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Touch ID & Password > Verify the Touch ID settings match your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/bioutil -r ; sudo /usr/bin/bioutil -r -s | /usr/bin/awk '/timeout/'

remediation.command: Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/bioutil -w -u <0,1> ; sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/bioutil -w -a <0,1> ; sudo usr/bin/bioutil -w -s -o <value≤172800>. GUI: System Settings > Touch ID & Password > Set the Touch ID settings to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Game Center Settings
description: With macOS 10.13, Apple has introduced a separate section for Game Center in System Settings. It is possible to log in with the Apple ID and use the iCloud-based Game Center services. Game Center is a feature from Apple that allows users to engage in game-related activities with friends when playing multiplayer games online on the Game Center social network.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.14.1 Audit Game Center Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has Allow GameCenter set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key allowGameCenter If the output is false, Game Center is disabled. If the output is true Game Center is enabled.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess allowGameCenter.

title: Audit Notification Settings
description: Notification capabilities are designed to allow users to receive updates from applications that are not currently in use. These can be background applications or even notices from processes running on a computer that is not currently being actively used.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.15.1 Audit Notification Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Notifications > Verify that Show previews for each application is set to your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Notifications > any applications that are not in compliance with your organization's requirements > Turn off or mute notifications that may expose information to unauthorized people that might be able to view screens of organizational computers.

title: Audit Wallet & Apple Pay Settings
description: Touch ID is a prerequisite for using Apple Pay and Wallet on macOS. Apple Pay allows an Apple account holder to enroll their credit cards in Apple Pay and pay enrolled vendors without using the physical card or number. Apple's service eliminates the requirement to send the credit card number itself to the vendor.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.16.1 Audit Wallet & Apple Pay Settings

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Wallet & Apple Pay > Verify the Wallet & Apple Pay settings match your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Wallet & Apple Pay > Set the Wallet & Apple Pay settings to your organization's requirements.

title: Audit Internet Accounts for Authorized Use
description: Apple provides a section in System Settings to create and display Internet Accounts. Setting up an Internet Account allows the user to configure access to pre-existing accounts that are Internet Accessible.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.17.1 Audit Internet Accounts for Authorized Use

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > Internet Accounts > Verify that all accounts are set to your organization's requirements.

remediation.command: GUI: System Settings > Internet Accounts > For each account, select the account > Verify that each sync option is set to your organization's requirements > (Optional) Select Delete Account... to remove the account > (Optional) Select Add Account... to add an account to the system.

title: Ensure On-Device Dictation Is Enabled
description: In macOS 14.0 Sonoma, Apple released the ability to limit dictation to staying on-device and not sending data to the Siri servers. The use of dictation is likely to include editing documents with confidential information. While Apple does have controls to obfuscate voice data that exists on their servers, it is recommended that Dictation-collected information does not leave the local Mac.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.18.1 Ensure On-Device Dictation Is Enabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.applicationaccess').objectForKey('forceOnDeviceOnlyDictation').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess forceOnDeviceOnlyDictation = <true/>.

title: Audit Software Inventory
description: With the introduction of Mac OS X 10.6.6, Apple added a new application, App Store, which resides in the Applications directory. This application allows a user with admin privileges and an Apple Account to browse Apple's online App Store, purchase (including no-cost purchases), and install new applications, bypassing Enterprise software inventory controls.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.6 Audit Software Inventory

audit.command: Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/system_profiler SPApplicationsDataType

remediation.command: Delete any unnecessary applications from the system.

title: Ensure Bonjour Advertising Services Is Disabled
description: Bonjour is an auto-discovery mechanism for TCP/IP devices which enumerates devices and services within a local subnet. DNS on macOS is integrated with Bonjour and should not be turned off, but the Bonjour advertising service can be disabled.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1 Ensure Bonjour Advertising Services Is Disabled

audit.command:
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript <<'EOS'
$.NSUserDefaults.alloc.initWithSuiteName('com.apple.mDNSResponder').objectForKey('NoMulticastAdvertisements').js
EOS

remediation.guidance: Profile (preferred): com.apple.mDNSResponder NoMulticastAdvertisements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.mDNSResponder.plist NoMulticastAdvertisements -bool true.

title: Audit Connected FAT32 and ExFAT Drives
description: While FAT32 and exFAT offer cross-platform convenience, they introduce critical security gaps. These formats do not support encryption without third-party products (on any platform). Consequently, FAT32 and exFAT should be reserved strictly for temporary, non-sensitive data transfers, while any sustained use or sensitive data storage should utilize APFS (Encrypted).
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.3.3 Audit Connected FAT32 and ExFAT Drives

audit.command: Terminal: diskutil list external | grep -E 'DOS_FAT_32|Microsoft Basic Data' Any FAT32 or ExFAT drives connected should meet your organization's existing device policies for external drives.

remediation.command: Any connected FAT32 or ExFAT volumes need to be audited to verify that they meet your organization's existing device policies for external drives.

title: Audit Show All Filename Extensions
description: A filename extension is a suffix added to a base filename that indicates the base filename's file format. This is intended for any user that logs into the GUI and has a home folder and not for service accounts. For the audit, we will continue to verify that every account with a home folder has filename extensions enabled.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.1.1 Audit Show All Filename Extensions

audit.command: GUI: Finder > Finder in the menu bar > Settings > Advanced > Verify that Show all filename extensions is set. Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults read /Users/<username>/Library/Preferences/.GlobalPreferences.plist AppleShowAllExtensions ; sudo -u firstuser /usr/bin/defaults read /Users/firstuser/Library/Preferences/.GlobalPreferences.plist AppleShowAllExtensions

remediation.command: Terminal: sudo -u <username> /usr/bin/defaults write /Users/<username>/Library/Preferences/.GlobalPreferences.plist AppleShowAllExtensions -bool true ; sudo killall Finder ; sudo -u seconduser /usr/bin/defaults write /Users/secondname/Library/Preferences/.GlobalPreferences.plist AppleShowAllExtensions -bool true. GUI: Finder > Finder in the menu bar > Settings > Advanced > Set Show all filename extensions to enabled.

title: Audit History and Remove History Items
description: Organizational management of user web browsing history is a challenge affected by multiple facets. Organizations should decide whether to manage browser history and how much history should be maintained.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.2 Audit History and Remove History Items

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has HistoryAgeInDaysLimit set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType | /usr/bin/grep HistoryAgeInDaysLimit | /usr/bin/tr -d ' ' The output will be HistoryAgeInDaysLimit = followed by your organizations requirements.

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari HistoryAgeInDaysLimit = <integer><1,7,14,31,365,36500></integer>.

title: Ensure Prevent Cross-site Tracking in Safari Is Enabled
description: There is a vast network of groups that collect, use, and sell user data. One method used to collect user data is pay and provide content and services for website owners. Along with that "assistance," the site owners also push tracking cookies on visitors. In many cases the help allows a content owner to keep the site up. The tracking cookies allow information brokers to track web users across visited sites. Audit: All three keys must be present: BlockStoragePolicy=2, WebKitPreferences.storageBlockingPolicy=1, WebKitStorageBlockingPolicy=1.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.4 Ensure Prevent Cross-site Tracking in Safari Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/tr -d ' ') || exit 1
if printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qx 'BlockStoragePolicy=2;' && printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qxF 'WebKitPreferences.storageBlockingPolicy=1;' && printf '%s
' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -qx 'WebKitStorageBlockingPolicy=1;'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari BlockStoragePolicy = <integer>2</integer>; com.apple.Safari WebKitPreferences.storageBlockingPolicy = <integer>1</integer>; com.apple.Safari WebKitStorageBlockingPolicy = <integer>1</integer>.

title: Audit Hide IP Address in Safari Setting
description: Public (Routable) IP addresses can be used to track people to their current location, including home and business addresses. While a valid IP address is necessary to load the site, the valid address does not need to be provided to known trackers and should be hidden.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.5 Audit Hide IP Address in Safari Setting

audit.command: GUI: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Privacy > Verify that Hide IP address from trackers is set to your organization's requirement. title: Ensure Advertising Privacy Protection in Safari Is Enabled
description: Apple provides a framework that allows advertisers to target Apple users and end-users with advertisements. While many people prefer that when they see advertising it is relevant to them and their interests, the detailed information that is data mining collected, correlated, and available to advertisers in repositories is often disconcerting.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.6 Ensure Advertising Privacy Protection in Safari Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep "WebKitPreferences.privateClickMeasurementEnabled" | /usr/bin/tr -d ' "'

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari WebKitPreferences.privateClickMeasurementEnabled = <true/>.

title: Ensure Show Full Website Address in Safari Is Enabled
description: Attackers use websites with malicious or unwanted content to exploit the user or the computer. Part of the attack chain is to lure someone to load their content rather than the desired content. In order to reduce the risk in interacting with unwanted content, the full website address should always be displayed in Safari.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.7 Ensure Show Full Website Address in Safari Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -E 'ShowFullURLInSmartSearchField' | /usr/bin/tr -d ' '

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari ShowFullURLInSmartSearchField = <true/>.

title: Audit AutoFill
description: AutoFill capabilities in a Web Browser are a feature to allow a user to avoid re-typing the same user information in every form that a user encounters. Part of the modern internet consists of vendors establishing a seemingly close relationship with as many users as possible to market to them, data-mine from them and sell their data to third- party data aggregators.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.8 Audit AutoFill

audit.command: GUI: System Settings > General > Device Management > Verify that an installed profile has safariAllowAutoFill set to your organization's requirements. Terminal: sudo /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript (JXA) reading NSUserDefaults suite com.apple.applicationaccess, key safariAllowAutoFill

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.applicationaccess safariAllowAutoFill = <<true>or<false>/>.

title: Audit Pop-up Windows
description: Browser pop-up windows have long been one of the most annoying delivery mechanisms of unwanted web content. The content can be unwanted content, including Not Safe For Work, or malicious content relying on a user interacting with the pop-up. Safari has a built-in capability to disable pop-ups that should be enabled.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.9 Audit Pop-up Windows

audit.command: GUI: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Websites > Pop-up Windows > Verify the websites listed in Allow pop-up windows on the website below:. are allowed according to your organization's requirements Verify that When visiting other websites is set to Block and Notify or Block.

remediation.command: GUI: Safari > Safari from the menu bar > Settings > Websites > Pop-up Windows > Set all websites to Block and Notify or Block, listed in Allow pop-up windows on the website below:, or select Remove to remove a website > Set that When visiting other websites is set to Block and Notify or Block.

title: Ensure Show Status Bar Is Enabled
description: The Status Bar in Safari shows the full URL of any link on hover. It protects the user from visiting sites where the domain has been obfuscated by allowing the user to review whether the link points to an unexpected location.
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15.0 Sequoia Benchmark v2.1.0 - 6.3.10 Ensure Show Status Bar Is Enabled

audit.command:
out=$(/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -E 'ShowOverlayStatusBar' | /usr/bin/tr -d ' '

remediation.command: Profile (preferred): com.apple.Safari ShowOverlayStatusBar = <true/>.
